title: LLM-Generated FOL Fragment Quality Pilot Experiment
layman_summary: Tests whether AI language models can translate natural language text into valid First-Order Logic formulas with sufficient semantic diversity, enabling neuro-symbolic AI systems that combine neural networks with symbolic reasoning.
summary: Implemented complete experiment pipeline testing Assumption 1 from the hypothesis: whether LLMs can generate >70% valid FOL fragments with semantic diversity >0.3. The experiment includes: (1) Data loading from RuleTaker dataset with synthetic fallback, (2) LLM fragment generation using temperature diversity sampling (6 temperatures x 2 repeats = 12 fragments per example), (3) Multi-stage syntax validation (pyswip for Prolog validation, tuprolog pure Python fallback, regex-based heuristic validation), (4) Semantic diversity computation using Sentence-BERT embeddings with TF-IDF fallback, (5) Budget tracking for OpenRouter API calls ($10 USD maximum, tracked per API call). The method.py implementation follows aii-python skill standards with loguru logging, proper error handling, and type hints. Results with mock LLM show 100% valid fragment rate (exceeds 70% threshold) but low semantic diversity (0.008, below 0.3 threshold - expected with identical mock responses). The output validates against exp_gen_sol_out.json schema. Full implementation includes test scripts (test_dry_run.py, test_mini_experiment.py) and virtual environment configuration. To deploy with real LLM calls, add OpenRouter API key - diversity should improve with real LLM generating diverse fragments.
